preamble: Eleven solutions are of a kind, one of them collectively, not further defined

clue.text: Get beast to go uphill

parts.note: to win something is to get it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going uphill means reading from the bottom to the top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Someone tries to coax a stubborn animal up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no definition in the clue: the preamble says eleven answers are of one kind, and this is one of the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A winkle is a small edible sea snail, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: CIA, NCA etc, with powers to use silver to displace cannabis

definitions.note: examples standing for a plural noun

indicators.note: one thing is put to use in place of another, so a swap is made
to displace something is to push it out and take its spot

parts.note: potencies are powers or strengths
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Spy and police bodies are given powers to seize silver in place of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The NCA is Britain's National Crime Agency. Take POTENCIES, remove POT and put AG in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: The CIA and the National Crime Agency are both government organisations of this type, so they serve as examples.

clue.text: Ferret around: is mud involved?

indicators.note: things turned around are moved out of their order
something involved is tangled and complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rooting about wonders whether they will get muddy.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the answer the preamble calls the collective one: rather than a single shellfish, it names the whole category.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means seafood generally, especially a platter of mixed shellfish, so it covers the whole group collectively.

clue.text: Small shirt holds little to note, or nothing at all

indicators.note: whatever holds something has it inside
'to' here means next to, so one piece is placed beside another

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
wee is Scottish and informal for little
a T is a kind of shirt, as in T-shirt
fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tiny shirt barely has room for a note, or holds nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Small shirt splits into two single letters, S for the size and T for the T-shirt, with the little word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA (short for 'sweet Fanny Adams') is British slang meaning absolutely nothing.

clue.text: It could be lobster pot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rich creamy soup, often made from lobster
second meaning: unglazed white porcelain, so a pot can be made of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobster pot' looks like the trap fishermen use; split it, and lobster is a soup flavour while pot is the ceramic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thick shellfish soup and fired but unglazed pottery, sometimes called biscuit ware.

clue.text: Marines dispersed throughout vessel

indicators.note: things scattered through something sit separately inside it

parts.note: a ship is a seagoing vessel
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Marines spread themselves out across a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters do not go in together: R and M are separated, each inserted at a different spot in SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is a small swimming crustacean, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Two chessmen, one of which captures a third

indicators.note: a piece that captures another takes it in, so the named piece holds the extra one

parts.note: the king and the pawn are two chess pieces
R is the chess notation for a rook, a third piece

explanation.surface: A chess move in which one piece takes another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of which' points to the second chessman, PAWN, which takes R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A king prawn is a large prawn, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Motor racing, timid? Unlikely

parts.note: F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as the letter I
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A racing driver who is nervous seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use the digit 1 as the letter I, so F1 becomes FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishy story is dubious or hard to believe, so the informal word works as a synonym of improbable.

clue.text: One gathers pearls from margins of sandbank in river delta, instead of its head

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of the first letter of a word
the margins of a thing are its edges, so only the outermost letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the word with its first letter removed so another can replace it

explanation.surface: Someone collects pearls along the banks of a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the R at the front of RIVER to give DIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl gatherers traditionally swim down unaided to collect oysters, which is exactly what a skin-diver does.

clue.text: Pound backs dollar

indicators.note: to back something is to come behind it, fixing which piece goes second

parts.note: the dollar sign $ resembles an S
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Sterling is supporting the US currency on the money markets.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound comes after the dollar, so S goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A squid is a ten-armed cephalopod, counted among the seafood the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Cook rapidly and boil heads

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: cook it fast and boil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe for the very thing it spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a ten-legged crustacean with claws, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Imposes the first of taxes to be extracted from Hebrews

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out and removed

parts.note: the Levites were the Hebrew tribe descended from Levi

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ruler demands taxes from the Hebrews.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of LEVITES.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a tax or fine is to impose it officially, so the third-person verb form matches.

clue.text: Diverge, argue, make up … friends at last, eternally

parts.note: a road that forks splits and diverges

indicators.note: what comes at the last of each word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Two friends drift apart, quarrel, then reconcile for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' applies to all four words before it, not just to friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for keeps means permanently, for ever, an idiom equivalent to forever.

clue.text: Boatman reported for watch

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, who would call himself I

explanation.surface: The setter's own name is spoken in reference to a timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in the clue stands for the setter, so it gives I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or observe it closely, so the verb works as a synonym.

clue.text: Female shellfish, easily caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, here within the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Shellfish are an easy catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Shellfish looks like the definition for the puzzle's theme, but here it only carries the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A she is a female animal or person, used as a noun as in 'is it a he or a she?'.

clue.text: Coarse material to add fire to dance

indicators.note: adding means attaching one item onto another

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Someone wants to put fire into a dance with rough fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as flames but means dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopsack is a loosely woven, rough fabric, originally the sacking used to bag hops.

clue.text: Caught fish with nowhere to leave boat!

indicators.note: having nowhere means lacking it, so that part goes

parts.note: a haddock is a sea fish
a dock is where a boat is left

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands a catch but has nowhere to moor.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DOCK off the end of HADDOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is to be tricked or caught out, so the past form means caught.

clue.text: Expert the right wing excluded from conclusive arguments

indicators.note: what is excluded is left out

parts.note: proofs are arguments that settle a question
the right-hand half of the word, as a wing of a building

explanation.surface: A specialist with right-wing views is shut out of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right wing' sounds political but means the right half of PROOFS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro is a professional, someone skilled and experienced, so it is an informal synonym.

clue.text: Oddly cold arms

indicators.note: taking things oddly means keeping the first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: odd-numbered letters counted across both words

explanation.surface: Someone's arms feel strangely chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clammy skin, which is a nice nod to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Filthy lout, not unknown, witnessed speaking

indicators.note: 'not' tells you a letter is absent

parts.note: a yob is British slang for a loutish young man
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

indicators.note: speaking means the word is said out, so its sound counts

parts.note: seen means witnessed

explanation.surface: A dirty-mouthed thug is caught on camera saying something.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the Y from YOB, then add a word that sounds like SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene language is indecent and offensive, the same sense as filthy talk.

clue.text: Factory ship processed missing parts of pot

indicators.note: processing raw material changes its form, so the letters are reworked
what is missing has been taken away

parts.note: taken as written
the three letters are taken out separately, wherever they sit

explanation.surface: A fish-processing vessel at sea has lost bits of its lobster pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, O and T from FACTORY SHIP, then rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayfish is a lobster-like freshwater crustacean, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Boatman unequalled

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to stand alone is to have no equal

explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is also the setter's name, so it suggests I or ME, as in 14 down; here it is just a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea snail with a shell lined with mother-of-pearl, one of the preamble's shellfish.

clue.text: Perform B major composition, part of opening

parts.note: to do is to perform

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician plays a piece in B major as part of a recital's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' and 'opening' both pretend to be musical; the opening is a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the upright post at the side of a doorway, so it is one component of that gap in a wall.

clue.text: Funny story, having Enigmatist its lead character

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters go astray

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Enigmatist is another Guardian setter; only his first letter is used

explanation.surface: A joke whose main character is the fellow crossword setter Enigmatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigmatist is a real fellow setter, which makes 'lead character' look like the hero of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc prized for eating and for pearls, one of the preamble's shellfish.

clue.text: Melt tip and root of eggplant stuffed into razor shell

indicators.note: something stuffed into another sits inside it
the root of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
the tip of something is its end

indicators.note: the shell of a word is its outside, just the first and last letters

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cookery step: put the end of an aubergine inside a razor clam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Razor shell' looks like the shellfish of the theme, but it only means the outside letters of razor.
explanation.definitionFit: To render fat is to melt it down to extract and clarify it, a cookery sense.

clue.text: "D'oh" sounds as if it could be "doe", pre-Middle English

indicators.note: pre means before, so one piece is put in front

indicators.text: sounds as if it could be
indicators.note: this says the word is chosen for how it sounds

parts.note: a doe is a female deer
ME is the abbreviation for Middle English

explanation.surface: A note on how Homer Simpson's catchphrase would have sounded before Middle English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D'oh' sounds like 'doe', a female deer, and DEAR sounds like DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay or annoyance, used when something goes wrong.

clue.text: The way this clue's solution goes, the editor might be drunk

parts.words: The way this clue's solution goes
parts.note: this entry runs downwards in the grid
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A setter jokes that the editor must have been drinking to pass this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at its own direction in the grid: being a down entry gives DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink that has been downed has been swallowed quickly, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Might put into speech

indicators.note: putting it into speech means saying it, so its sound counts

parts.note: muscle means strength or might

explanation.surface: Someone could set something into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb but is the noun for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is a dark-shelled bivalve mollusc, one of the shellfish the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Finding a place for octopus in gastronomic display

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters straddling three words
surface padding, completing the picture of a food display

explanation.surface: A chef works out where to fit an octopus in a food display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is both a hiding signal and one of the hiding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding a place for something means putting it to use, so the present participle matches.

clue.text: Freely flow with abuse to make Spooner go crazy

indicators.note: letters set free can fall into any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A torrent of abuse would drive the Reverend Spooner mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner, famous for swapping initial sounds, is a hint: swap the B and F and the answer says 'flow abuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow a fuse is an idiom for losing your temper, so it means to go into a rage.

clue.text: See 3
Bend, use handle and let go

indicators.note: bending something twists it out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a lever: bend it, use the handle, and release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let go' is the definition and works as a past participle, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unleashed has been freed from restraint, like a dog off its lead.
